note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 4327 / 出力 2364 トークン

data.question: Should we adopt block_k 3 → 2 (rejected by B and C), adopt hold_limit 60s → 70s (on-time gain seen on only 1 of 5 seeds), or keep the current rules (v2)?
data.background: Option 1 passed every machine check and raises mean on-time by +2.2, but Companies B and C voted against it. Overriding a majority of affected companies is a matter for humans to agree, not for me. Option 2 passed the checks and the vote, but its +2.0 mean gain comes from only 1 of 5 seeds, so whether it really helps the main goal is uncertain. In D2 you treated 2/5 seeds as too weak to act on, and I should not set a lower bar on my own.

options.summary: Adopt block_k 3 → 2. On-time rises from 220.6 to 222.8 (+2.2, 1/5 seeds improved) and late falls from 2.2 to 0.0. Blocked s falls from 1322 to 946, and the lowest on-time rate rises from 0.98 to 1.00. Customer monitors improve: p95_wait_s 98.4 → 76.4, max_wait_s 146 → 128, unfinished stays 0.0. Road violations rise from 23.4 to 33.6. Adopting it would override the votes of B and C (A ○, B ×, C ×).
options.stakeholders: Customers gain shorter waits (p95 and max) and no late deliveries. A gains (utility 73.8 → 76.0). B loses (73.6 → 55.0). C loses heavily (45.4 → 28.2), after C already lost in D1. Other road users bear about 44% more road violations.

options.summary: Adopt hold_limit 60s → 70s. On-time rises from 220.6 to 222.6 (+2.0), but only 1/5 seeds improved. Late falls from 2.2 to 0.2, and the lowest on-time rate rises to 1.00. Customer monitors improve: p95_wait_s 98.4 → 89.0, max_wait_s 146 → 139, unfinished stays 0.0. Road violations fall from 23.4 to 21.0, but blocked s rises from 1322 to 1429. It passed the vote (A ○, B ×, C ○).
options.stakeholders: Customers gain moderately shorter waits on average, though the gain may not hold on most demand patterns. A gains (73.8 → 75.8) and C gains (45.4 → 48.4). B loses slightly (73.6 → 73.0). Robots spend more time blocked (+107 s).

options.summary: Stay at v2. On-time stays at 220.6, late at 2.2, p95_wait_s at 98.4, max_wait_s at 146, unfinished at 0.0, and road violations at 23.4.
options.stakeholders: Customers keep the current service: nearly all orders on time, with somewhat longer waits than under either option. Company utilities stay at A 73.8 / B 73.6 / C 45.4. No company loses, and none gains.

recommendation.reason: Neither option's main-goal gain is robust: both improve on-time on only 1 of 5 seeds, which is weaker evidence than the 2/5 you rejected in D2. Option 1 would also override B and C and push C's utility from 45.4 to 28.2 after C already lost in D1, while road violations rise by about 44%. Option 2 has no measured harm to customers and improves the customer monitors, but its mean gain likely comes from a single seed. Re-measuring it with more seeds or under this period's demand would be a better basis than adopting it now. The current rules already deliver 220.6 on time with 2.2 late and 0.0 unfinished.
assumptions: The 5 seeds represent this period's demand well enough that a 1/5 improvement rate means the gain is not reliable.
The mean gains of +2.2 and +2.0 come mostly from one favourable seed rather than from small gains spread across seeds.
Under the current rules, conditions next period will stay close to the measured current row.
Company C's repeated utility losses matter as a tie-breaker, as in D2, even though fairness is not part of the KPI.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: No rule change, so it should stay around 220.6 under the same demand.

unknowns: Whether option 2's gain holds with more seeds or under next period's demand; only 5 seeds were measured, and 1 improved.
How the on-time gains are distributed across seeds, for example whether one seed accounts for most of the mean.
Why B voted against option 2 despite only a small utility drop, and whether B and C would accept option 1 with some compensation.
How customers perceive waits shortened by about 10–20 s compared with the current service.
Next period's demand level, and whether block_k 3 → 2 behaves differently in a busy period.
How companies would change their behaviour once a rule is adopted, since the measurements assume fixed policies.
Whether the extra road violations under option 1 carry safety or third-party costs that are not in the KPI.
